name: Co Lung duck
summary: Cổ Lũng duck is the bird Bản Hiêu and Vietnam Airlines both treat as a valley specialty: little fat, boiled, grilled, roasted, or xáo. Vịt cỏ on the Bản Đôn list is not called the same bird. A current price is Check on arrival.
origin: VnExpress, 18 Jun 2023, places the breed at Bản Hiêu, then at xã Cổ Lũng: short legs, a round body, brown feathers mixed with black, a short thick neck, and a white ring. The 3 Jul 2023 VnExpress account says sparrow-colored feathers and the same white ring. Both descriptions stand. Vietnam Airlines calls it a specialty breed only at Pù Luông.
texture: VnExpress, 18 Jun 2023, quotes a valley roast-duck shopkeeper: firm, sweet, thick meat, little fat, and no foul smell. The skin is described as crisp, and the color as a deep brown close to honey.
taste: VnExpress, 3 Jul 2023, says even the boiled bird is sweet, fragrant, and firm. Vietnam Airlines says the meat is fragrant and low in fat.
howToEat: Order it boiled, grilled, or roasted. Vietnam Airlines also names xáo and does not define that word. A recipe for xáo is Check on arrival.

The 16 May 2022 market article dips boiled Cổ Lũng duck in chẩm chéo. The 18 Jun 2023 account also names a dip of pounded duck liver, salt, and mắc khén, and boiled duck with chili-lime salt. Locals on that account use chẩm chéo with a little fried garlic.

On 18 Jun 2023 VnExpress quoted Lò Văn Huyên, head of Bản Hiêu, at 100,000–150,000 đồng a kilogram for a live bird, and about 200,000–350,000 đồng for a grilled, boiled, or roasted bird of about 1.2–2 kg. A current price is Check on arrival.

where: Bản Hiêu and xã Cổ Lũng, and the stilt-house meal. A shop door was not printed. Check on arrival.
culture: The 18 Jun 2023 account says the breed has a long history at Bản Hiêu and was later raised in xã Cổ Lũng, along streams such as Nậm Bá, Pù Luông, and Pha Lé. Feed named there: chopped wild banana, corn, rice from the fields, and small stream animals.
